title: Luck
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; Word File German translations suggested separately

entries.description: When bad things keep happening to you by chance
To make fortunate or unfortunate things happen, e.g. a black cat
What you do with closed eyes before blowing out birthday candles
When a dream really happens
When things go well or badly for you by chance
To hope very much that you will get something
Strange and a bit scary, like a ghost story
To think that magic signs like black cats can change your fortune

entries.example: I really didn't want to get up when my alarm clock rang.
entries.description: It rings in the morning to wake you up
You ask this to find out if someone was successful

entries.example: Mr Wallis, the teacher, arrives and sits down beside them.
entries.description: Next to
A polite way to ask if something is OK for someone

entries.example: Candyman is an evil spirit.
entries.description: Very bad and wicked, like a witch in a fairy tale
You say this when you were only being funny

entries.example: Ignore him - he's just being silly.
entries.description: To pay no attention to someone

entries.example: I am not really satisfied with your answer.
entries.description: Happy because you got what you wanted

entries.example: I heard your scream in the middle of the night.
entries.description: A very loud, high cry when you are scared

entries.example: Nick is lying in his sleeping bag.
entries.description: You lie in this in a tent at night

entries.example: There is a spirit by the name of Candyman.
entries.description: A ghost; a being without a body

entries.example: It's only a silly superstition, after all.
entries.description: An old belief like 'Breaking a mirror brings bad fortune'

entries.example: If you whistle, you'll attract rain.
entries.description: To make something come to you, like a magnet

entries.example: When you want to enter your home, you have to turn sharply to the left or right.
entries.description: To go into a room or a building

entries.example: If you get a haircut before an exam, you'll forget everything.
entries.description: You get this at the barber's

entries.example: Isn't it obvious that you should watch your handbag carefully?
entries.description: Very easy to see or understand

entries.example: Traditional homes in China have large spirit screens.
entries.description: Done the same way for a very long time

entries.example: Some homes in China have spirit screens to trick ghosts.
entries.description: To make someone believe something that isn't true

entries.example: In Italy, the unlucky number is 17.
entries.description: Bringing bad fortune, like the number 13 for some people

entries.example: If you whistle when the sun is shining, it will shine for more than two hours.
entries.description: To make a high sound by blowing air through your lips

entries.example: You'll have bad luck if you walk on the cracks in the pavement.
entries.description: A thin line where something has broken a little

entries.example: I can hear a cuckoo in the woods.
entries.description: A bird that calls its own name; also a kind of clock

entries.example: I sometimes don't walk on the cracks in the pavement.
entries.description: The path for people at the side of a street

entries.example: You'll get rich if you hear a cuckoo and shake your money.
entries.description: Having a lot of money

entries.example: I always shake the money in my pocket if I hear a cuckoo.
entries.description: To move something quickly up and down

entries.example: Are you superstitious?
entries.description: Describes a person who thinks black cats bring bad fortune

entries.example: If you don't wear a jacket, you'll catch a cold.
entries.description: To get ill with a runny nose and a sore throat

entries.example: If you drop your toothbrush, you'll have to wash it.
entries.description: You clean your teeth with it

entries.example: Have you got something else arranged?
entries.description: To plan or organise something with someone
You say this when you have no doubt

entries.example: I just found a lucky charm.
entries.description: A small object that people think brings good fortune

entries.example: Oh no, I spilled the salt on the table.
entries.description: The white seasoning that goes with pepper

entries.example: You seriously believe in all these things?
entries.description: Really, truly; not as a joke
